front_desk.title: Front Desk
front_desk.responsibility: Give Engineering a clear account of what a guest or coworker reported. Keep the guest and the next desk shift informed as the work moves forward.
front_desk.shift: Read Staff Notes, review open tickets, and check Pool Status or Weather before advising guests. When a new issue comes in, record the exact room or location, what the guest observed, and when Engineering can get access.
front_desk.workflow: Your report starts the repair. Updates on the same ticket help Engineering plan the visit and give the desk a reliable status for the next callback.

phases.title: Start with the facts
phases.text: Use + Work Order. Enter your first name, the exact location, and what happened. Add a photo when useful, then select Submit Request.

phases.title: Check for a matching report
phases.text: Review possible duplicates from the same room or location before submitting. If the problem is already on file, open that ticket and add the new information there.

phases.title: Link a finding from an inspection
phases.text: A scheduled inspection can start the same workflow. Engineering records the finding in Preventive Maintenance and follows the fix in the linked work order.

phases.title: Verify and prioritize
phases.text: A report that needs verification starts in Pending Verification. Engineering checks the location, issue, priority, and equipment before it goes to Open. Use the ticket and its notifications to follow that change.

phases.title: Open the job and coordinate access
phases.text: Open the source ticket, read its status, and confirm assignment and access before promising a repair time. Use any available room or location tools for the latest context.

phases.title: Investigate and record the repair
phases.text: Use Notes & Ticket History to check earlier work and clarify access, the original symptom, or the guest impact. Engineering keeps the technical findings and outcome on the same ticket.

phases.title: Follow parts and supply needs
phases.text: A repair can pause while Engineering checks inventory, orders a part, or waits for a shipment. Use the ticket’s parts information and latest notes when coordinating a follow-up.

phases.title: Document, review, and close
phases.text: Use the recorded outcome to see what changed and what remains. Completed is ready for review. Closed confirms the final disposition, and further work goes through the authorized reopening path.

phases.title: Hand off the result
phases.text: Read the recorded outcome before giving an update. Use Staff Notes for the handoff and include the ticket number.

actions.title: Enter your first name

screenshot.alt: Create Work Order in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Choose a room or location

manager.title: General Manager
manager.responsibility: Oversee maintenance that affects guests, room availability, or more than one department. Use the property’s shared records to see what still needs attention.
manager.shift: Review urgent or recurring work, room moves and out-of-order rooms, and the pending items in Staff Notes. Use GSS Reports, PM, and read-only Manage Locations to understand broader impact.
manager.workflow: Connect the desk, Housekeeping, and Engineering around access, room availability, and guest commitments. Keep the coordination on the ticket so everyone can follow Engineering’s progress.

phases.title: Start with the facts
phases.text: Create a work order for a new issue. On an existing ticket, add the business or guest impact and correct a report detail when the control is available.

phases.title: Check for a matching report
phases.text: Review possible duplicates from the same room or location before submitting. If the problem is already on file, open that ticket and add the new information there.

phases.title: Link a finding from an inspection
phases.text: In Preventive Maintenance, an inspection finding can point to a linked work order. The PM record keeps the check and finding. The ticket carries assignment, repair, and verification. Use the work-order link or approved request action when your controls allow it.

phases.title: Verify and prioritize
phases.text: A report that needs verification starts in Pending Verification. Engineering checks the location, issue, priority, and equipment before it goes to Open. Use the ticket and its notifications to follow that change.

phases.title: Open the job and coordinate access
phases.text: Open Work Order List for urgent work and compare the ticket’s location with Daily Room Ops if room access or availability is at stake.

phases.title: Investigate and record the repair
phases.text: Open the demo ticket and review its reported issue and history. Use the Guest Room Troubleshooting Guide to find the matching issue checks, then keep any results and next action on the ticket.

phases.title: Follow parts and supply needs
phases.text: Check Inventory before requesting an order. Use the applicable purchase view to track expected shipments. If your controls allow receiving, record only what physically arrived. Keep the ticket’s parts status current.

phases.title: Document, review, and close
phases.text: Use the recorded outcome to see what changed and what remains. Completed is ready for review. Closed confirms the final disposition, and further work goes through the authorized reopening path.

phases.title: Hand off the result
phases.text: Review the recorded resolution and remaining follow-ups. Carry any outstanding decisions into the next management handoff.

lessons.title: Create Work Order
lessons.purpose: Create Work Order sends a maintenance issue to the property’s work queue with a specific room or location and a clear description.
lessons.when: Open it when you find a new problem or receive a report that needs someone to investigate.

actions.title: Open Create Work Order
actions.text: Use the + Work Order shortcut on your dashboard whenever a new issue needs to enter the shared work queue.
actions.hint: Click the outlined + Work Order button to open the form.

screenshot.alt: Create Work Order in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Choose a room or location
actions.text: Choose the exact guest room, fixture, or common area. The sample uses Room 204.
actions.hint: Click Room / Location and choose the matching result.

screenshot.alt: Create Work Order in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Describe the observed issue
actions.text: Enter the symptom or problem. A specific short description helps Engineering distinguish it from other work in that room.
actions.hint: Click Issue and type the observed fault.

screenshot.alt: Create Work Order in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Add access or follow-up notes
actions.text: Record useful guest context, when staff may enter, and any action already taken.
actions.hint: Click Notes / Actions Taken to record the extra details.

screenshot.alt: Create Work Order in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Enter the report together
actions.text: You can also paste the location, fault, and guest or access notes together in Issue. The saved ticket shows the fault under Reported Issue.
actions.hint: Use the outlined Issue box for one combined report.

screenshot.alt: Create Work Order in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Check the detected room
actions.text: CMPRI recognizes the location in this example and selects Room 204. Confirm the highlighted location, especially for common areas or reports with more than one room.
actions.hint: Check Room / Location before continuing.

screenshot.alt: Create Work Order in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Check the report before it creates a ticket

actions.hint: Click the outlined submit button to see the sample duplicate check.

screenshot.alt: Create Work Order in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Confirm the separated issue

actions.hint: Read the clean issue and confirm it matches the reported fault.

screenshot.alt: Create Work Order in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Confirm the separated notes

screenshot.alt: Create Work Order in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Review the possible duplicate

lessons.title: Pool Status
lessons.purpose: The Pool Status window shows whether the pool is open and displays the current closure reason when it is closed.
lessons.when: Check before advising a guest or whenever a closure notice arrives.

actions.title: Open Pool Status
actions.text: Select the Pool Status button in the dashboard header to see the current state and available controls.
actions.hint: Click the highlighted Pool Status button.

screenshot.alt: Pool Status in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Verify the current state
actions.text: Read the current pool state and any displayed reason before advising guests or handing over pool coverage.

screenshot.alt: Pool Status in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Record a closure reason
actions.text: If the pool must close, follow the property’s pool-closure procedure. Enter the specific reason so the next shift knows what needs attention.
actions.hint: Use the Closure reason field.

screenshot.alt: Pool Status in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Select Close pool
actions.text: Submit the closure after entering its cause. Check that CMPRI now displays CLOSED and retains the reason.
actions.hint: Use Close pool beside the reason field.

screenshot.alt: Pool Status in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Verify the closure and hand it off
actions.text: The status and reason are visible here. Tell the next shift why the pool is closed and check this state before telling guests that it is available.

screenshot.alt: Pool Status in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Request an authorized reopening
actions.text: After the cause is resolved, use Open pool and read the confirmation. Current tests must pass and operating hours must permit opening. A passing retest leaves an independent manual hold in place.
actions.hint: Open pool uses a confirmation before requesting that CMPRI clear the hold.

screenshot.alt: Pool Status in CMPRI with sample data

lessons.title: Pool Log
lessons.purpose: Pool Log records the property’s water test results, daily checks, retests, and actions taken.
lessons.when: Open it when you are responsible for a scheduled test or need to see the last verified readings.

actions.title: Verify the log date
actions.text: Confirm the date at the top before entering readings. Where a facility selector is present, select the facility you actually tested first.

screenshot.alt: Pool Log in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Review today’s activity
actions.text: Read the saved samples and actions in chronological order before choosing a new test.

screenshot.alt: Pool Log in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Enter the sample pH

screenshot.alt: Pool Log in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Enter the same sample’s bromine

screenshot.alt: Pool Log in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Correct a saved entry

screenshot.alt: Pool Log in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Correct only the recorded mistake

screenshot.alt: Pool Log with Editing saved log expanded in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Save Pool Log

actions.title: Recognize a result that requires closure
actions.text: The sample PM pH of 8.0 is above the allowed 7.2–7.8 range. CMPRI also requires closure for unsafe bromine readings, loss of main-drain visibility, or water above 104°F.

actions.title: Record what you did

actions.title: Save the failed test

assistant_manager.title: Assistant General Manager
assistant_manager.responsibility: Keep departments coordinated during your shift and cover Manager duties as assigned, including front-desk applicant review and pool operations.
assistant_manager.shift: Review the desk handoff and outstanding room issues. Check Room Ranker and GSS Reports when a room problem affects guest plans. Record a pool test or review winter readiness when your coverage includes those duties.
assistant_manager.workflow: Connect department leads when a repair depends on access, room availability, or a guest decision. Record who needs to follow up and the ticket that has the full history.

phases.title: Start with the facts
phases.text: For a new issue, use + Work Order and enter your first name, location, and issue. For an existing ticket, add timing or access information.

phases.title: Check for a matching report
phases.text: Review possible duplicates from the same room or location before submitting. If the problem is already on file, open that ticket and add the new information there.

phases.title: Link a finding from an inspection
phases.text: A scheduled inspection can start the same workflow. Engineering records the finding in Preventive Maintenance and follows the fix in the linked work order.

phases.title: Verify and prioritize
phases.text: A report that needs verification starts in Pending Verification. Engineering checks the location, issue, priority, and equipment before it goes to Open. Use the ticket and its notifications to follow that change.

phases.title: Open the job and coordinate access
phases.text: Check Work Order List and Staff Notes for open risks, outstanding promises, and the department already handling each issue.

phases.title: Investigate and record the repair
phases.text: Open the demo ticket and review its reported issue and history. Use the Guest Room Troubleshooting Guide to find the matching issue checks, then keep any results and next action on the ticket.

phases.title: Follow parts and supply needs
phases.text: A repair can pause while Engineering checks inventory, orders a part, or waits for a shipment. Use the ticket’s parts information and latest notes when coordinating a follow-up.

phases.title: Document, review, and close
phases.text: Use the recorded outcome to see what changed and what remains. Completed is ready for review. Closed confirms the final disposition, and further work goes through the authorized reopening path.

phases.title: Hand off the result
phases.text: Check Engineering’s recorded outcome. Pass open room or guest commitments to the next supervisor in Staff Notes.

lessons.title: Review a Work Order

Notes & Ticket History opens by default in CMPRI. This walkthrough starts with every section collapsed so you can see how each opens. Select Next to see Reported Issue.

lessons.title: Pool Status
lessons.purpose: The Pool Status window shows whether the pool is open and displays the current closure reason when it is closed.
lessons.when: Check before advising a guest or whenever a closure notice arrives.

actions.title: Open Pool Status
actions.text: Select the Pool Status button in the dashboard header to see the current state and available controls.
actions.hint: Click the highlighted Pool Status button.

screenshot.alt: Pool Status in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Verify the current state
actions.text: Read the current pool state and any displayed reason before advising guests or handing over pool coverage.

screenshot.alt: Pool Status in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Record a closure reason
actions.text: If the pool must close, follow the property’s pool-closure procedure. Enter the specific reason so the next shift knows what needs attention.
actions.hint: Use the Closure reason field.

screenshot.alt: Pool Status in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Select Close pool
actions.text: Submit the closure after entering its cause. Check that CMPRI now displays CLOSED and retains the reason.
actions.hint: Use Close pool beside the reason field.

screenshot.alt: Pool Status in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Verify the closure and hand it off
actions.text: The status and reason are visible here. Tell the next shift why the pool is closed and check this state before telling guests that it is available.

screenshot.alt: Pool Status in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Request an authorized reopening
actions.text: After the cause is resolved, use Open pool and read the confirmation. Current tests must pass and operating hours must permit opening. A passing retest leaves an independent manual hold in place.
actions.hint: Open pool uses a confirmation before requesting that CMPRI clear the hold.

screenshot.alt: Pool Status in CMPRI with sample data

lessons.title: Pool Log
lessons.purpose: Pool Log records the property’s water test results, daily checks, retests, and actions taken.
lessons.when: Open it when you are responsible for a scheduled test or need to see the last verified readings.

actions.title: Verify the log date
actions.text: Confirm the date at the top before entering readings. Where a facility selector is present, select the facility you actually tested first.

screenshot.alt: Pool Log in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Review today’s activity
actions.text: Read the saved samples and actions in chronological order before choosing a new test.

screenshot.alt: Pool Log in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Enter the sample pH
actions.text: Choose the pH for your AM or PM sample. An earlier saved sample stays in the log.

screenshot.alt: Pool Log in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Enter the same sample’s bromine
actions.text: Choose the bromine range from the same sample. CMPRI records one shared result for shallow and deep.

screenshot.alt: Pool Log in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Correct a saved entry
actions.text: Use Edit saved log only when an earlier entry needs a correction. Add a new paired sample through the AM or PM inputs or use Record another test.

screenshot.alt: Pool Log in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Correct only the recorded mistake
actions.text: Use Edit saved log to correct an existing entry you are authorized to edit. Use an available AM or PM sample field or Record another test for newly collected water.
actions.hint: Editing saved log indicates that earlier fields are unlocked.

screenshot.alt: Pool Log with Editing saved log expanded in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Save Pool Log
actions.text: Save the completed sample and check the resulting status. If CMPRI calls for closing the pool, follow the displayed instructions and hand off the reason.

screenshot.alt: Pool Log in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Recognize a result that requires closure
actions.text: The sample PM pH of 8.0 is above the allowed 7.2–7.8 range. CMPRI also requires closure for unsafe bromine readings, loss of main-drain visibility, or water above 104°F.
actions.hint: Select Next to see how to record the failed test.

screenshot.alt: Pool Log in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Record what you did
actions.text: Use Notes / actions taken to record the situation and the actions you completed before saving the log.

screenshot.alt: Pool Log in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Save the failed test
actions.text: Save the reading and the actions you took. An out-of-range result automatically sets the CMPRI pool status to Closed and records the reason.
actions.hint: Select Next to check the dashboard.

screenshot.alt: Pool Log in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Check the dashboard status
actions.text: Pool Status in the upper-right corner shows Closed. Open it to read the reason. Eligible staff see in-app alerts and receive push notifications on phones and in browsers when enabled.
actions.hint: Select Next to see what keeps the pool closed.

screenshot.alt: Pool Log in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Check what keeps the pool closed
actions.text: The pool stays closed until required tests pass, daily checks are complete, operating hours permit opening, and applicable holds are cleared.
actions.hint: Select Next to continue.

screenshot.alt: Pool Log in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Read Pool Specs
actions.text: This reference shows required flow and what the daily log records. Use it when checking what measurements to collect.

screenshot.alt: Pool Log with Pool Specs expanded in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Record a retest
actions.text: Use Record another test for a new paired pH and bromine reading. The earlier AM and PM results stay in the history.

screenshot.alt: Pool Log with Additional shared test expanded in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Review the daily checks
actions.text: Temperature, flow, drain visibility, and backwash are daily checks. Check which values are already recorded before adding missing information.

screenshot.alt: Pool Log with Additional shared test expanded in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Choose the chemical that was used
actions.text: Chemical usage shows eligible inventory stored in the Pool Pump Room. Select the item you actually used.

screenshot.alt: Pool Log with Chemical usage expanded in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Record actual usage
actions.text: Enter the amount and unit used, then select Add chemical use. The stock change is applied when the pool log is saved.

screenshot.alt: Pool Log with Chemical usage expanded in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Review earlier logged readings
actions.text: View entire pool log opens the saved entries with the newest first. Scroll through the table for previous tests, daily checks, and closure reasons.
actions.context: Entire pool log · Indoor Pool · Expanded

screenshot.alt: Pool Log with Entire pool log · Indoor Pool expanded in CMPRI with sample data

lessons.purpose: Room Ranker groups guest rooms by A, B, or C using active work-order priorities and counts. C needs the most attention.
lessons.when: Check it when coordinating room assignments, turnover, inspections, or repair priorities.

actions.title: Read the room-rank totals
actions.text: Count active work orders tied to the same guest room. Pending Verification, Open, and In Progress count. Completed, Closed, and Will Not Do are excluded.

actions.hint: Tap 1st Floor or select Next.

actions.text: Room 110 starts with one active Medium work order. Its room rank is B.

screenshot.alt: Room Ranker with 1st Floor expanded in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Find the original report

actions.hint: Tap +1 more or select Next to see the first ticket.

screenshot.alt: Room Ranker with 1st Floor expanded in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: The first ticket remains Medium
actions.text: The first ticket remains Medium. Two active Medium tickets keep a room at B. The leading ticket in this example was entered as Urgent.

actions.title: Confirm Urgent on the work order

actions.title: Recognize automatic escalation
actions.text: Separate sample. The red mark flags an automatic priority increase. Three original Medium tickets or four original Low tickets in the same room become Urgent. Three Low tickets rise to Medium.

actions.title: Read the escalated priorities

lessons.title: Weather
lessons.purpose: Weather shows current conditions, forecasts, radar, and active weather alerts for the property area.
lessons.when: Check it before weather-sensitive work, guest advisories, or shift preparation.

actions.title: Check current conditions
actions.text: Read the temperature and observation time before weather-sensitive work, travel coordination, or a guest advisory.

screenshot.alt: Weather in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Read the official alert for the hazard
actions.text: Guest Safety displays applicable official NWS alerts in CMPRI. Follow the specific hotel action. In a Cold Weather Advisory, offer guests a warm indoor waiting area and minimize time outdoors.

screenshot.alt: Weather in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Spot a watch below the dashboard header
actions.text: A watch means conditions could develop. The yellow bulletin sits under the dashboard header and shows the hazard and expiration. Select it to open Guest Safety.

screenshot.alt: Weather in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Read the watch and its timing
actions.text: Watch and advisory details open in a compact Guest Safety window. Check the effective and expiration times in Central time.

screenshot.alt: Weather in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Prepare entrances and sidewalks
actions.text: Use the Winter Storm Watch to check entrances and guest walkways and get ice melt ready. Open Winter Preparedness 2026 to confirm who will clear snow and treat sidewalks, and make sure supplies are staged before conditions worsen.

screenshot.alt: Weather in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Recognize the full-screen warning
actions.text: A warning signals a hazard is happening or imminent. CMPRI opens full-screen Guest Safety for an applicable warning. Follow the hotel action immediately.

screenshot.alt: Weather in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Direct staff and guests to shelter
actions.text: For a Tornado Warning, direct staff and guests immediately to the first-floor interior hallways, away from windows and exterior doors.

screenshot.alt: Weather in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Read the full bulletin
actions.text: Expand Official NWS bulletin text to review the complete message and the hazard instructions. This capture uses a sample bulletin.

screenshot.alt: Weather with Official NWS bulletin text expanded in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Reopen the active warning from the dashboard
actions.text: The red bulletin stays below the dashboard header after you close Weather or Guest Safety. Select it to reopen details while the alert is active.

screenshot.alt: Weather in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Show the radar layer
actions.text: Select Reflectivity and any other map layers you need.

screenshot.alt: Weather in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Inspect radar around the property
actions.text: Zoom and recenter to inspect the area, or compare observed frames with the loop control below the map.

screenshot.alt: Weather in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Play the observed radar loop
actions.text: Play the loop or move its frame slider to see how observed conditions changed over time.

screenshot.alt: Weather in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Plan ahead for snow, ice, and cold
actions.text: Check the hourly forecast for snow, freezing rain, and freezing temperatures. If ice is expected, coordinate sidewalk treatment with the shift lead and use Staff Notes to tell coworkers which entrances need attention.

screenshot.alt: Weather in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Recognize simulated preparation messages
actions.text: Select Open notifications in Weather to see Weather Prep and Winter Prep, which are simulated forecast heads-ups for practice. Plan real snow and ice work using the hourly forecast and Winter Preparedness checklist.

screenshot.alt: Weather in CMPRI with sample data

front_desk_manager.title: Front Desk Manager
front_desk_manager.responsibility: Lead front-desk maintenance follow-up and guest communication. Coordinate property access with Engineering and review front-desk candidate questionnaires.
front_desk_manager.shift: Check Staff Notes and the open work list. Use Room Ranker and GSS Reports to spot guest-impacting concerns. Help desk staff report clear issues, record scheduled pool readings when assigned, and use Hours Tracker for your own hours.
front_desk_manager.workflow: Turn desk requests into actionable reports with accurate room, access, and guest details. Give desk staff a clear next action while Engineering owns the technical work.

phases.title: Start with the facts
phases.text: Use + Work Order for a new issue and identify yourself by first name. Add guest updates, photos, or access details to an existing ticket.

phases.title: Check for a matching report
phases.text: Review possible duplicates from the same room or location before submitting. If the problem is already on file, open that ticket and add the new information there.

phases.title: Link a finding from an inspection
phases.text: A scheduled inspection can start the same workflow. Engineering records the finding in Preventive Maintenance and follows the fix in the linked work order.

phases.title: Verify and prioritize
phases.text: A report that needs verification starts in Pending Verification. Engineering checks the location, issue, priority, and equipment before it goes to Open. Use the ticket and its notifications to follow that change.

phases.title: Open the job and coordinate access
phases.text: Read the ticket’s status and notes before promising access or repair timing. Notify the desk team when their next action changes.

phases.title: Investigate and record the repair
phases.text: Open the demo ticket and review its reported issue and history. Use the Guest Room Troubleshooting Guide to find the matching issue checks, then keep any results and next action on the ticket.

phases.title: Follow parts and supply needs
phases.text: A repair can pause while Engineering checks inventory, orders a part, or waits for a shipment. Use the ticket’s parts information and latest notes when coordinating a follow-up.

phases.title: Document, review, and close
phases.text: Use the recorded outcome to see what changed and what remains. Completed is ready for review. Closed confirms the final disposition, and further work goes through the authorized reopening path.

phases.title: Hand off the result
phases.text: Confirm the documented result and whether a guest callback or room assignment is still due. Share the handoff with a ticket reference.

housekeeping.title: Lead Housekeeper
housekeeping.responsibility: Lead housekeeping’s maintenance reporting during room checks and turnover. Let Front Desk and Engineering know when a defect affects room readiness.
housekeeping.shift: Review Room Ranker, work orders, and Staff Notes. When a room check uncovers a problem, capture the specific location and what you found, plus a helpful photo or the time the room is available.
housekeeping.workflow: Your reports help Engineering identify the repair. Room-access and readiness updates let Housekeeping and Front Desk coordinate around the same work order.

phases.title: Start with the facts
phases.text: Choose the room and explain what you found. Attach a photo when it clarifies the fault, then select Submit Request for Engineering verification.

phases.title: Check for a matching report
phases.text: Review possible duplicates from the same room or location before submitting. If the problem is already on file, open that ticket and add the new information there.

phases.title: Link a finding from an inspection
phases.text: A scheduled inspection can start the same workflow. Engineering records the finding in Preventive Maintenance and follows the fix in the linked work order.

phases.title: Verify and prioritize
phases.text: A report that needs verification starts in Pending Verification. Engineering checks the location, issue, priority, and equipment before it goes to Open. Use the ticket and its notifications to follow that change.

phases.title: Open the job and coordinate access
phases.text: Add access or turnover timing to the existing ticket. Use Staff Notes when the desk or the next housekeeping shift needs the update.

phases.title: Investigate and record the repair
phases.text: Use Notes & Ticket History to check earlier work and clarify access, the original symptom, or the guest impact. Engineering keeps the technical findings and outcome on the same ticket.

phases.title: Follow parts and supply needs
phases.text: A repair can pause while Engineering checks inventory, orders a part, or waits for a shipment. Use the ticket’s parts information and latest notes when coordinating a follow-up.

phases.title: Document, review, and close
phases.text: Use the recorded outcome to see what changed and what remains. Completed is ready for review. Closed confirms the final disposition, and further work goes through the authorized reopening path.

phases.title: Hand off the result
phases.text: Review the recorded repair before passing a readiness update to Front Desk. Add what you observe if an issue still needs attention.

technician.title: Maintenance Technician
technician.responsibility: Handle assigned work and eligible unassigned jobs. Record what you checked, what you repaired, and what needs more time, parts, or access.
technician.shift: Open the Technician Dashboard and check the Work Order List, room access, and inspections due. Record technical findings, complete assigned PM and pool tasks, and hand off anything still in progress.
technician.workflow: Your notes and status changes give Engineering leadership a record to review and let other departments coordinate access or guest communication around the repair.

phases.title: Start with the facts
phases.text: Start a work order with the exact room or location and the observed issue. Keep guest information, access instructions, and follow-up in the notes so the issue stays easy to read.

phases.title: Check for a matching report
phases.text: Review possible duplicates from the same room or location before submitting. If the problem is already on file, open that ticket and add the new information there.

phases.title: Link a finding from an inspection
phases.text: In Preventive Maintenance, an inspection finding can point to a linked work order. The PM record keeps the check and finding. The ticket carries assignment, repair, and verification. Use the work-order link or approved request action when your controls allow it.

phases.title: Verify and prioritize
phases.text: A report that needs verification starts in Pending Verification. Engineering checks the location, issue, priority, and equipment before it goes to Open. Use the ticket and its notifications to follow that change.

phases.title: Open the job and coordinate access
phases.text: Review assigned work first. If an unassigned ticket is eligible and you can take it, claim it under your name.

phases.title: Investigate and record the repair
phases.text: Review the reported issue, equipment, and earlier tests. Use the diagnostic guidance available to you, then record what you checked, what you fixed, and any remaining work in the ticket.

phases.title: Follow parts and supply needs
phases.text: Check Inventory before requesting an order. Use the applicable purchase view to track expected shipments. If your controls allow receiving, record only what physically arrived. Keep the ticket’s parts status current.

phases.title: Document, review, and close
phases.text: Use the recorded outcome to see what changed and what remains. Completed is ready for review. Closed confirms the final disposition, and further work goes through the authorized reopening path.

phases.title: Hand off the result
phases.text: Use the ticket for the recorded repair outcome and Staff Notes for the next shift’s follow-up. Include the room and work-order number.

chief_engineer.title: Chief Engineer
chief_engineer.responsibility: Lead the maintenance queue, verify reports, coordinate assignments, and review repair completion and PM follow-up.
chief_engineer.shift: Check Work Order Approvals and the urgent work list first. Review Daily Room Ops for access, PM for inspections and deficiencies, and inventory or purchase orders for repair blockers. Coordinate team coverage and handoffs in Staff Notes.
chief_engineer.workflow: Turn staff reports and PM findings into clear, prioritized jobs. Preserve the verification, repair, and closure decisions in the ticket so departments can see what changed.

phases.title: Start with the facts
phases.text: Start a work order with the exact room or location and the observed issue. Keep guest information, access instructions, and follow-up in the notes so the issue stays easy to read.

phases.title: Check for a matching report
phases.text: Review possible duplicates from the same room or location before submitting. If the problem is already on file, open that ticket and add the new information there.

phases.title: Link a finding from an inspection
phases.text: In Preventive Maintenance, an inspection finding can point to a linked work order. The PM record keeps the check and finding. The ticket carries assignment, repair, and verification. Use the work-order link or approved request action when your controls allow it.

phases.title: Verify and prioritize
phases.text: Open Work Order Approvals. Check the location, reported issue, potential duplicates, priority, and equipment. Approve the request into Open when ready.

phases.title: Open the job and coordinate access
phases.text: Assign a technician or leave eligible work available to claim. Coordinate access, equipment guidance, and parts for the investigation.

phases.title: Investigate and record the repair
phases.text: Review the reported issue, equipment, and earlier tests. Use the diagnostic guidance available to you, then record what you checked, what you fixed, and any remaining work in the ticket.

phases.title: Follow parts and supply needs
phases.text: Check Inventory before requesting an order. Use the applicable purchase view to track expected shipments. If your controls allow receiving, record only what physically arrived. Keep the ticket’s parts status current.

phases.title: Document, review, and close
phases.text: Review the completed record and work performed before closing it. Use the authorized follow-up, disposition, or reopening path when the recorded result calls for more work.

phases.title: Hand off the result
phases.text: Use the ticket for the recorded repair outcome and Staff Notes for the next shift’s follow-up. Include the room and work-order number.

actions.title: Save Work Order

lessons.title: Pool Status
lessons.purpose: The Pool Status window shows whether the pool is open and displays the current closure reason when it is closed.
lessons.when: Check before advising a guest or whenever a closure notice arrives.

actions.title: Open Pool Status
actions.text: Select the Pool Status button in the dashboard header to see the current state and available controls.
actions.hint: Click the highlighted Pool Status button.

screenshot.alt: Pool Status in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Verify the current state
actions.text: Read the current pool state and any displayed reason before advising guests or handing over pool coverage.

screenshot.alt: Pool Status in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Record a closure reason
actions.text: If the pool must close, follow the property’s pool-closure procedure. Enter the specific reason so the next shift knows what needs attention.
actions.hint: Use the Closure reason field.

screenshot.alt: Pool Status in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Select Close pool
actions.text: Submit the closure after entering its cause. Check that CMPRI now displays CLOSED and retains the reason.
actions.hint: Use Close pool beside the reason field.

screenshot.alt: Pool Status in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Verify the closure and hand it off
actions.text: The status and reason are visible here. Tell the next shift why the pool is closed and check this state before telling guests that it is available.

screenshot.alt: Pool Status in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Reopen after the cause is resolved
actions.text: Select Open pool and confirm clearing the manual closure. CMPRI keeps the pool closed if required tests still fail or hours do not permit opening.
actions.hint: Open pool uses a confirmation before requesting that CMPRI clear the hold.

screenshot.alt: Pool Status in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Verify the pool reopened
actions.text: Check that CMPRI actually shows OPEN before announcing that the pool is available.

screenshot.alt: Pool Status in CMPRI with sample data

lessons.title: Pool Log
lessons.purpose: Pool Log records the property’s water test results, daily checks, retests, and actions taken.
lessons.when: Open it when you are responsible for a scheduled test or need to see the last verified readings.

actions.title: Verify the log date
actions.text: Confirm the date at the top before entering readings. Where a facility selector is present, select the facility you actually tested first.

screenshot.alt: Pool Log in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Review today’s activity
actions.text: Read the saved samples and actions in chronological order before choosing a new test.

screenshot.alt: Pool Log in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Enter the sample pH
actions.text: Choose the pH for your AM or PM sample. An earlier saved sample stays in the log.

screenshot.alt: Pool Log in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Enter the same sample’s bromine
actions.text: Choose the bromine range from the same sample. CMPRI records one shared result for shallow and deep.

screenshot.alt: Pool Log in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Save Pool Log
actions.text: Save the completed sample and check the resulting status. If CMPRI calls for closing the pool, follow the displayed instructions and hand off the reason.

screenshot.alt: Pool Log in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Recognize a result that requires closure
actions.text: The sample PM pH of 8.0 is above the allowed 7.2–7.8 range. CMPRI also requires closure for unsafe bromine readings, loss of main-drain visibility, or water above 104°F.
actions.hint: Select Next to see how to record the failed test.

screenshot.alt: Pool Log in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Record what you did
actions.text: Use Notes / actions taken to record the situation and the actions you completed before saving the log.

screenshot.alt: Pool Log in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Save the failed test
actions.text: Save the reading and the actions you took. An out-of-range result automatically sets the CMPRI pool status to Closed and records the reason.
actions.hint: Select Next to check the dashboard.

screenshot.alt: Pool Log in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Read the saved result
actions.text: The saved result retains the failed reading and gives the closure instruction. Check Pool Status and communicate the cause to the next shift.

screenshot.alt: Pool Log in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Check the dashboard status
actions.text: Pool Status in the upper-right corner shows Closed. Open it to read the reason. Eligible staff see in-app alerts and receive push notifications on phones and in browsers when enabled.
actions.hint: Select Next to see what keeps the pool closed.

screenshot.alt: Pool Log in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Check what keeps the pool closed
actions.text: The pool stays closed until required tests pass, daily checks are complete, operating hours permit opening, and applicable holds are cleared.
actions.hint: Select Next to continue.

screenshot.alt: Pool Log in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Read Pool Specs
actions.text: This reference shows required flow and what the daily log records. Use it when checking what measurements to collect.

screenshot.alt: Pool Log with Pool Specs expanded in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Record a retest
actions.text: Use Record another test for a new paired pH and bromine reading. The earlier AM and PM results stay in the history.

screenshot.alt: Pool Log with Additional shared test expanded in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Review the daily checks
actions.text: Temperature, flow, drain visibility, and backwash are daily checks. Check which values are already recorded before adding missing information.

screenshot.alt: Pool Log with Additional shared test expanded in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Choose the chemical that was used
actions.text: Chemical usage shows eligible inventory stored in the Pool Pump Room. Select the item you actually used.

screenshot.alt: Pool Log with Chemical usage expanded in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Record actual usage
actions.text: Enter the amount and unit used, then select Add chemical use. The stock change is applied when the pool log is saved.

screenshot.alt: Pool Log with Chemical usage expanded in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Review earlier logged readings
actions.text: View entire pool log opens the saved entries with the newest first. Scroll through the table for previous tests, daily checks, and closure reasons.
actions.context: Entire pool log · Indoor Pool · Expanded

screenshot.alt: Pool Log with Entire pool log · Indoor Pool expanded in CMPRI with sample data

lessons.title: Room Ranker
lessons.purpose: Room Ranker groups guest rooms by A, B, or C using active work-order priorities and counts. C needs the most attention.
lessons.when: Check it when coordinating room assignments, turnover, inspections, or repair priorities.

actions.title: Read the room-rank totals
actions.text: Count active work orders tied to the same guest room. Pending Verification, Open, and In Progress count. Completed, Closed, and Will Not Do are excluded.

screenshot.alt: Room Ranker in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Open the floor
actions.text: Choose 1st Floor to find the room, its rank, and its leading work order.
actions.hint: Tap 1st Floor or select Next.

screenshot.alt: Room Ranker in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: One Medium ticket · Rank B
actions.text: Room 110 starts with one active Medium work order. Its room rank is B.

screenshot.alt: Room Ranker with 1st Floor expanded in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Two tickets · Rank C

screenshot.alt: Room Ranker with 1st Floor expanded in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Find the original report
actions.text: The +1 more button gives you the other active work order for this room.
actions.hint: Tap +1 more or select Next to see the first ticket.

screenshot.alt: Room Ranker with 1st Floor expanded in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: The first ticket remains Medium
actions.text: The first ticket remains Medium. Two active Medium tickets keep a room at B. The leading ticket in this example was entered as Urgent.
actions.hint: Select Next to return to the floor and open its leading issue.

screenshot.alt: Room Ranker in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Open the leading issue
actions.text: Select Water running onto the bathroom floor to open WO#4232 and check its priority.
actions.hint: Tap the highlighted issue or select Next.

screenshot.alt: Room Ranker with 1st Floor expanded in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Confirm Urgent on the work order
actions.text: The Urgent Priority badge confirms the second ticket was entered as Urgent. Room Ranker uses that active ticket to place Room 110 at rank C.

screenshot.alt: Room Ranker in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Recognize automatic escalation
actions.text: Separate sample. The red mark flags an automatic priority increase. Three original Medium tickets or four original Low tickets in the same room become Urgent. Three Low tickets rise to Medium.

actions.title: Read the escalated priorities

engineer.title: Engineer
engineer.responsibility: Diagnose maintenance faults, use verified equipment documentation, and apply the technical editing and review rights granted to your account.
engineer.shift: Prioritize open work, check room access, and review prior findings before investigating. Record results, track parts needs, and check for inspection or repair follow-up.
engineer.workflow: Keep technical findings with the job so the Chief Engineer and technicians can continue the work. Other departments use your updates to understand availability and the next action.

phases.title: Start with the facts
phases.text: Start a work order with the exact room or location and the observed issue. Keep guest information, access instructions, and follow-up in the notes so the issue stays easy to read.

phases.title: Check for a matching report
phases.text: Review possible duplicates from the same room or location before submitting. If the problem is already on file, open that ticket and add the new information there.

phases.title: Link a finding from an inspection
phases.text: In Preventive Maintenance, an inspection finding can point to a linked work order. The PM record keeps the check and finding. The ticket carries assignment, repair, and verification. Use the work-order link or approved request action when your controls allow it.

phases.title: Verify and prioritize
phases.text: Use Work Order List and any authorized approvals controls to check the location, issue, technical details, and priority.

phases.title: Open the job and coordinate access
phases.text: Open the source ticket, read its status, and confirm assignment and access before promising a repair time. Use any available room or location tools for the latest context.

phases.title: Investigate and record the repair
phases.text: Review the reported issue, equipment, and earlier tests. Use the diagnostic guidance available to you, then record what you checked, what you fixed, and any remaining work in the ticket.

phases.title: Follow parts and supply needs
phases.text: Check Inventory before requesting an order. Use the applicable purchase view to track expected shipments. If your controls allow receiving, record only what physically arrived. Keep the ticket’s parts status current.

phases.title: Document, review, and close
phases.text: Review the completed record and work performed before closing it. Use the authorized follow-up, disposition, or reopening path when the recorded result calls for more work.

phases.title: Hand off the result
phases.text: Use the ticket for the recorded repair outcome and Staff Notes for the next shift’s follow-up. Include the room and work-order number.

senior_management.title: Senior Management
senior_management.responsibility: Review property maintenance and guest-impact trends using work orders, room operations, GSS Reports, and PM. Your role can also maintain locations and submit new pool readings or retests.
senior_management.shift: Review high-impact or recurring work. Check operational reports and Staff Notes for context, and use the review views for purchasing, inventory, and equipment when they help explain a blocker.
senior_management.workflow: Use the work-order history to follow decisions with property leadership and Engineering. Add relevant context to a permitted ticket and follow the responsible team’s resolution.

phases.title: Start with the facts
phases.text: Start a work order with the exact room or location and the observed issue. Keep guest information, access instructions, and follow-up in the notes so the issue stays easy to read.

phases.title: Check for a matching report
phases.text: Review possible duplicates from the same room or location before submitting. If the problem is already on file, open that ticket and add the new information there.

phases.title: Link a finding from an inspection
phases.text: In Preventive Maintenance, an inspection finding can point to a linked work order. The PM record keeps the check and finding. The ticket carries assignment, repair, and verification. Use the work-order link or approved request action when your controls allow it.

phases.title: Verify and prioritize
phases.text: A report that needs verification starts in Pending Verification. Engineering checks the location, issue, priority, and equipment before it goes to Open. Use the ticket and its notifications to follow that change.

phases.title: Open the job and coordinate access
phases.text: Use Work Order List and Rooms & Reports to connect repair trends with room availability and guest impact.

phases.title: Investigate and record the repair
phases.text: Use Notes & Ticket History to check earlier work and clarify access, the original symptom, or the guest impact. Engineering keeps the technical findings and outcome on the same ticket.

phases.title: Follow parts and supply needs
phases.text: Check Inventory before requesting an order. Use the applicable purchase view to track expected shipments. If your controls allow receiving, record only what physically arrived. Keep the ticket’s parts status current.

phases.title: Document, review, and close
phases.text: Use the recorded outcome to see what changed and what remains. Completed is ready for review. Closed confirms the final disposition, and further work goes through the authorized reopening path.

phases.title: Hand off the result
phases.text: Confirm the recorded repair or disposition and bring remaining property-level concerns to the appropriate leadership handoff.

system_admin.responsibility: Maintain authorized system access and property records. Apply full technical or review controls when the property needs authorized support or coverage.
system_admin.shift: Check Manage Users and Feedback for account or support needs. Verify role and property membership, then use relevant work-order, equipment, location, or operations records to troubleshoot.
system_admin.workflow: Give staff access appropriate to their duties and preserve a clear record when resolving issues that affect work. Coordinate technical changes with Engineering and property leadership.

phases.title: Start with the facts
phases.text: Start a work order with the exact room or location and the observed issue. Keep guest information, access instructions, and follow-up in the notes so the issue stays easy to read.

phases.title: Check for a matching report
phases.text: Review possible duplicates from the same room or location before submitting. If the problem is already on file, open that ticket and add the new information there.

phases.title: Link a finding from an inspection
phases.text: In Preventive Maintenance, an inspection finding can point to a linked work order. The PM record keeps the check and finding. The ticket carries assignment, repair, and verification. Use the work-order link or approved request action when your controls allow it.

phases.title: Verify and prioritize
phases.text: Check the account’s property and role and open the affected ticket or linked record. Read existing activity before making any corrections.

phases.title: Open the job and coordinate access
phases.text: Use Work Order Approvals to verify requests or provide assignment and status coverage when Engineering needs help.

phases.title: Investigate and record the repair
phases.text: Review the reported issue, equipment, and earlier tests. Use the diagnostic guidance available to you, then record what you checked, what you fixed, and any remaining work in the ticket.

phases.title: Follow parts and supply needs
phases.text: Check Inventory before requesting an order. Use the applicable purchase view to track expected shipments. If your controls allow receiving, record only what physically arrived. Keep the ticket’s parts status current.

phases.title: Document, review, and close
phases.text: Review the completed record and work performed before closing it. Use the authorized follow-up, disposition, or reopening path when the recorded result calls for more work.

phases.title: Hand off the result
phases.text: Use the ticket for the recorded repair outcome and Staff Notes for the next shift’s follow-up. Include the room and work-order number.

lessons.title: Create Work Order
lessons.purpose: Create Work Order sends a maintenance issue to the property’s work queue with a specific room or location and a clear description.
lessons.when: Open it when you find a new problem or receive a report that needs someone to investigate.

actions.text: Use the + Work Order shortcut on your dashboard whenever a new issue needs to enter the shared work queue.

actions.title: Choose a room or location

actions.title: Describe the observed issue

lessons.title: Pool Log
lessons.purpose: Pool Log records the property’s water test results, daily checks, retests, and actions taken.
lessons.when: Open it when you are responsible for a scheduled test or need to see the last verified readings.

actions.title: Verify the log date
actions.text: Confirm the date at the top before entering readings. Where a facility selector is present, select the facility you actually tested first.

screenshot.alt: Pool Log in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Review today’s activity
actions.text: Read the saved samples and actions in chronological order before choosing a new test.

screenshot.alt: Pool Log in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Enter the sample pH
actions.text: Choose the pH for your AM or PM sample. An earlier saved sample stays in the log.

screenshot.alt: Pool Log in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Enter the same sample’s bromine
actions.text: Choose the bromine range from the same sample. CMPRI records one shared result for shallow and deep.

screenshot.alt: Pool Log in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Correct a saved entry
actions.text: Use Edit saved log only when an earlier entry needs a correction. Add a new paired sample through the AM or PM inputs or use Record another test.

screenshot.alt: Pool Log in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Correct only the recorded mistake
actions.text: Use Edit saved log to correct an existing entry you are authorized to edit. Use an available AM or PM sample field or Record another test for newly collected water.
actions.hint: Editing saved log indicates that earlier fields are unlocked.

screenshot.alt: Pool Log with Editing saved log expanded in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Save Pool Log

screenshot.alt: Pool Log in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Recognize a result that requires closure
actions.text: The sample PM pH of 8.0 is above the allowed 7.2–7.8 range. CMPRI also requires closure for unsafe bromine readings, loss of main-drain visibility, or water above 104°F.
actions.hint: Select Next to see how to record the failed test.

screenshot.alt: Pool Log in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Record what you did
actions.text: Use Notes / actions taken to record the situation and the actions you completed before saving the log.

screenshot.alt: Pool Log in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Save the failed test

screenshot.alt: Pool Log in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Check the dashboard status
actions.text: Pool Status in the upper-right corner shows Closed. Open it to read the reason. Eligible staff see in-app alerts and receive push notifications on phones and in browsers when enabled.

lessons.title: Feedback
lessons.purpose: Send a problem report, bug report, or suggestion about CMPRI.
lessons.when: Use Feedback to report an issue with CMPRI or suggest an improvement. Use a work order for property or equipment repairs.

actions.title: Choose the type of feedback
actions.text: Use Problem, Bug, or Suggestion to identify the kind of CMPRI issue you want to report.

screenshot.alt: Feedback in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Describe what happened
actions.text: Provide the steps and the result you saw. Use a work order when the issue is with the property or equipment.

screenshot.alt: Feedback in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Send the feedback
actions.text: After reviewing the description, choose Submit. CMPRI includes the originating page and app version.

screenshot.alt: Feedback in CMPRI with sample data

lessons.title: Connect ChatGPT
lessons.purpose: Connect ChatGPT opens the CMPRI profile’s connection section for a per-user, permissions-scoped connection.
lessons.when: Use it when you want to connect your own account and your role offers the connection.

actions.title: Check your connection status
actions.text: A disconnected sample account shows Not connected. This launcher opens Manage Profile.

screenshot.alt: Connect ChatGPT in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Open the connection setup
actions.text: Choose Connect ChatGPT to review the account-specific setup steps.

screenshot.alt: Connect ChatGPT in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Review the secure OAuth setup
actions.text: Read the account requirements before connecting ChatGPT to CMPRI.

screenshot.alt: Connect ChatGPT in CMPRI with sample data

actions.title: Copy the endpoint in CMPRI
actions.text: In the live app, copy the endpoint and use the approved OAuth steps for your own authorized account.

screenshot.alt: Connect ChatGPT in CMPRI with sample data

lessons.title: Sign Out
lessons.purpose: Sign Out ends your CMPRI session on this device.
lessons.when: Use it when finishing work on a shared device or handing it over to another account.

actions.title: Select Sign Out
actions.text: Use Account → Sign Out at the end of your shift, especially on a shared property computer.

screenshot.alt: Sign Out in CMPRI with sample data
